skill.name: ai-handler
skill.description: Build Replicate AI generation workflows with Inngest background jobs, S3 storage, database state, and credit handling.
skill.summary: Pattern for Replicate AI jobs with queues, storage, status tracking, and credits.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: Most static high and medium signals are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, headings, and TypeScript examples rather than executable skill behavior. The skill still demonstrates real server-side network fetching of Replicate output and lacks important validation, timeout, and credit atomicity safeguards in the documented pattern.

remediation.issue: Server-side fetch of model output lacks validation controls.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist trusted Replicate output hosts, require expected content types, enforce byte limits, and reject redirects to private networks before upload.

remediation.issue: Credit deduction, record creation, and job dispatch are not atomic in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Use a database transaction with an outbox pattern or idempotent job creation, and refund credits automatically when enqueue or processing fails.

remediation.issue: Prediction polling has no documented timeout or maximum retry count.
remediation.suggestion: Add a deadline, maximum attempts, and failure status update, or prefer Replicate webhooks for long-running predictions.

remediation.issue: The Replicate token handling is only shown as a minimal SDK example.
remediation.suggestion: Document that tokens must remain server-only, never be logged, and must not be exposed to client bundles or job payloads.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Server-Side Output Fetch
semantic_findings.description: The worker fetches finalPrediction.output[0] server-side and buffers the full response before upload. Without URL allowlisting, content-type checks, and size limits, this pattern can create SSRF-like outbound requests or memory pressure if the output URL is unsafe.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly fetches a URL from model output and converts the full response into memory. Replicate output is usually legitimate, so the confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Non-Atomic Credit Deduction And Job Dispatch
semantic_findings.description: The example creates a record, deducts credits, and sends the Inngest event as separate operations. If dispatch fails after deduction, users can be charged for work that was never queued.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sequence is visible in the API route and no transaction, outbox, or idempotency guard is shown. The skill is a pattern document, so implementation details may vary.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Prediction Polling Loop
semantic_findings.description: The polling loop waits until Replicate returns succeeded or failed, but it does not show a maximum attempt count or timeout. A stuck prediction could keep jobs active and consume worker capacity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The loop condition and sleep are shown without a termination bound. This is an operational denial-of-service risk, although Inngest or Replicate limits may reduce impact.

content.value_statement: Long-running AI jobs need durable state, billing, and asset storage. This skill shows a Replicate pipeline with Inngest processing, S3 persistence, and credit handling.
actual_capabilities: Outlines an authenticated API route for AI generation requests.
Shows credit checks and optimistic credit deduction before queueing work.
Creates a database generation record with processing, completed, and failed states.
Defines an Inngest worker that starts and polls Replicate predictions.
Downloads Replicate output and uploads it to S3 for persistent storage.
Updates database records after successful or failed background processing.
limitations: Provides implementation patterns, not a complete ready-to-run application.
Requires existing Replicate, Inngest, S3, database, authentication, and credit helpers.
Does not include full webhook handling, migrations, or provider-specific model schemas.
Does not show complete validation for prompts, output URLs, file size, or content type.

use_cases.title: Add AI image generation to a SaaS app
use_cases.description: Use the pattern to accept generation requests, charge credits, queue work, and return processing status.

use_cases.title: Move slow model calls into background jobs
use_cases.description: Adapt the Inngest worker flow for predictions that take longer than an API request should handle.

use_cases.title: Persist AI results for later retrieval
use_cases.description: Store temporary Replicate output in S3 and update database rows with stable asset URLs.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a basic Replicate image generation flow. Include authentication, credit checking, record creation, and background job dispatch.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a model worker
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for a chosen Replicate model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the worker pattern for my Replicate model. Account for my model output format, S3 upload, status updates, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a working implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my current AI generation pipeline with this skill. Identify missing retry, timeout, refund, validation, and storage controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design production controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for scale and reliability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design production controls for this Replicate workflow. Cover webhooks, idempotent credits, output URL validation, observability, and abuse prevention.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to add Replicate image generation to a Next.js app.
output: A request flow with authentication, credit check, record creation, and background dispatch.
A worker flow that calls Replicate, waits for completion, uploads to S3, and updates status.
A failure path that marks the job failed and explains where refunds should occur.

output_examples.input: A product engineer asks why generated images should be copied to S3.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that provider output URLs can be temporary, so the application should persist generated assets under its own storage policy.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer asks how to make the workflow safer for production.
output: Add output URL allowlists, content-type checks, and size limits before upload.
Use bounded polling or webhooks to avoid stuck workers.
Make credit deduction and job dispatch idempotent.

best_practices: Validate prompt length, model parameters, output URLs, content type, and file size before storing results.
Use idempotent job keys, bounded retries, and automatic refunds for failed generations.
Keep provider tokens server-only and never include secrets in client code or job payloads.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch arbitrary model output URLs without host, redirect, size, and content checks.
Do not store only temporary Replicate URLs when users need durable access to generated assets.
Do not deduct credits without a reliable refund or compensation path for failed jobs.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build a Replicate generation pipeline with API intake, background processing, S3 persistence, database state, and credits.

faq.question: Does it include complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript patterns that must be adapted to an existing app, schema, and helper libraries.

faq.question: Which services does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes Replicate for model inference, Inngest for background work, S3 for storage, and a database for generation state.

faq.question: Can it support models that do not return images?
faq.answer: Yes, but the worker and storage logic must be changed for the model output type.

faq.question: What security controls should be added?
faq.answer: Add prompt validation, output URL allowlists, content limits, bounded polling, secret protection, and idempotent credit handling.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
